status_note: Launched 2026-08-07T18:18Z on av2 and av3, both hosts complete by 2026-08-08T03:49Z, closed 2026-08-10. Written at launch with everything already fixed, and completed on close with the decision, the closing timestamp, the row counts and the rescoring split below. Nothing here is inferred from an mtime.
kind_note: A standard gen_configs.py / run_experiments.py / merge_experiments.py repair campaign, run once per path against two separate CSVs. The only factor is genetic.elitism_rate, carried by sweep R on both paths. Unusually for this repo the campaign re-runs a factor an earlier campaign already carried: `replicate` (2026-07-31) crossed sweep R as a nuisance variable, and 6000 of its rows were recovered from av2/av3 and analysed before this one was designed. See PLAN.md section 3 for that prior and the three reasons it does not close the question.
question: Whether the shipped `genetic.elitism_rate` default should be 0.0 or 0.1. This is a production-defaults question rather than a search-behaviour one: counter is meant to be push-button, so the default has to hold across a corpus rather than on the spec that motivated it. The design argument says 0.0 — both NSGA-II schemes pool survivors (mu+lambda) and are already elitist, and elites bypass the offspring filter chain including the vacuity and well-separation screens. Against it stood one measurement, n=1, on examples/lily02 at seed 42, where elitism_rate = 0 returned a repair whose guarantee reduced to `true`. That anecdote is what include/config.hpp and example-config.toml currently cite as the reason the default stays at 0.1.
decision: Keep genetic.elitism_rate = 0.1. Two of the four pre-registered criteria fail, so the shipped default stands. Criterion 4 (cost): elitism 0 runs 16.2% longer on TLSF and 8.2% on FRETISH, and the rule allows 10%. Criterion 3 (triviality): the elit0 arm wrote 3 tautological repairs, so it is not zero -- but the elit0.1 arm wrote 4, so this is the screen defect the rule anticipated rather than an elitism result, and it is reported as such. Criteria 1 and 2 pass on both paths. Notably the direction on outcomes favours 0 rather than 0.1 wherever the two differ, so the default is kept on cost, not on quality: the trade is +3.3pp TLSF yield for +16% wall time. The n=1 lily02 anecdote that previously justified this default is retired -- see include/config.hpp, rewritten in the closing commit.
decision_rule: Pre-registered in PLAN.md section 7, before any row at this commit was collected. Switch the default to 0.0 only if all four hold: (1) upper bound of the 95% CI on the implies_ideal difference below +0.05 absolute on both paths; (2) the same on found_repair; (3) zero trivial repairs in the elit0 arm under the post-hoc ltlfilt audit; (4) mean wall_time_s at 0.0 no more than 10% above 0.1 on both paths. Otherwise keep 0.1 and rewrite the justification comment in include/config.hpp and example-config.toml to cite this campaign and the criterion that failed, replacing the n=1 lily02 anecdote. The prior data predicts criterion 4 is the one that fails, at a wall ratio of 0.87-0.88.

profile_commit.subject: chore(experiments): add elitism-default campaign profiles and plan
profile_commit.held_by_tag_note: The branch was rebased onto main after the campaign ran, so 4ea255b and 2ebe3a9 are no longer reachable from any branch. The annotated tag provenance/elitism-campaign points at 2ebe3a9 and holds both, plus the vendored script blobs. Never delete it: without it git gc collects them and every sha this file names stops resolving.

profile_commit_evidence: Both hosts were reset to origin/feat/elitism-campaign and rebuilt before launch; `counter --version` reads commit=4ea255b, dirty=0 on both. run_experiments.py's own launch gate refuses a binary whose commit differs from the working tree's HEAD or was built dirty, and it was left on — no --allow-stale-binary. Every CSV row carries the commit and dirty columns independently.

binary_commit.source: counter --version, captured on both hosts after the pre-launch rebuild

rescored_at.scope: FRETISH only (results-elitism.csv), 927 of 1200 rows -- every row that produced repairs. results-elitism-tlsf.csv is untouched.
rescored_at.why: compare loaded every .json in the repairs directory, including the run.json manifest write_run_manifest leaves there, threw on it, and aborted the whole comparison. The runner recorded that as best_relation=unknown, implies_ideal=0, so the FRETISH quality metric read as a flat zero rather than as an error. Fixed in 2ebe3a9 on this branch; the GA runs themselves are untouched and still carry commit=4ea255b in every CSV row, which is correct -- only the compare-derived columns were recomputed. The TLSF path was immune because its repairs are .tlsf and the manifest is .json.
rescored_at.method: scripts/recompare.py --results experiments/results-elitism.csv, run on each host against the retained run directories; 463 rows on av2, 464 on av3, 0 failed.

engine_commits_that_motivated_the_rerun.why: added the tautology screen to the vacuity filter; decides exactly the `G true` guarantee case the lily02 anecdote exhibited
rescue correct offspring only when filters empty the population
resolve realizability timeouts as undecided rather than unrealizable
flipped run_well_separation and allow_output_assumptions to true; well-separation interacts with elitism directly, since elites bypass the offspring filter chain that applies it

design.sweep: R (FRETISH) and TLSF sweep R — the same letter because it is the same factor
design.scheme: nsga2-truncate only, not crossed; it is the shipped default and the question is about the shipped configuration

elitism-tlsf.jobs_note: jobs=1 for the same RAM reason as every other TLSF profile: max_concurrent_realizability is per-process, so concurrent counter processes multiply peak ltlsynt residency

design.config_deviation_from_shipped_defaults: gen_configs.py's baseline pins the fitness weights at 0.33/0.33/0.1/0.33 rather than config.hpp's 0.2/0.5/0.1/0.5, plus model_counting.default_bound = 20 and runtime.black_timeout_ms = 1000. These are campaign conventions shared with every prior sweep; changing them here would make this campaign incomparable with the replicate rows it re-tests. Under nsga2-truncate the weights only select which components are active — all four are non-zero either way — so they do not bias selection and reach only the reported best_fitness scalar, which is not among the outcomes. run_vacuity and run_well_separation are deliberately left unpinned so both take the binary's current default of true.

host_split.method: seed-major, disjoint, never by spec or arm — so a host lost mid-campaign still leaves a balanced design over every spec and arm
host_split.hostname_note: The per-host manifest filename uses the machine's real hostname, not the ssh alias, so av2's manifest is results-elitism-manifest-avlab12.json
host_split.phase_order: FRETISH first, then TLSF, sequentially on each host. The two never co-schedule: the FRETISH arm runs jobs=4 and the TLSF arm jobs=1, and overlapping them would contaminate wall_time_s, which is criterion 4 of the decision rule.

run_window.note: av3's clock runs ~17 minutes fast with NTP off. No figure in this campaign derives from cross-host timestamps, so the skew is recorded and left uncorrected, as in 2026-08-06-wellsep-timing.

caveats: The TLSF quality pass is largely a floor effect. Only 6 of the 20 families ever score implies_ideal at all; the other 14 read 0 in both arms and contribute denominators only. Restricted to the 6 informative families (239 pairs) the difference is -0.025 with a 95% CI of [-0.081, +0.030] -- same direction, three times wider, and no longer inside the 0.05 margin. Criterion 1 on TLSF is 'not contradicted' rather than 'established'.

FRETISH implies_ideal existed only after the rescore. Before it, all 927 rows with repairs read best_relation=unknown and implies_ideal=0, which is a measurement failure that looks exactly like a legitimate result on every other column. Any analysis of this CSV predating 2026-08-10 is wrong on the FRETISH quality axis.

The 7 tautological repairs are a black soundness bug, not an elitism finding, and are reported as such per the pre-registered rule. They are also the reason to distrust any weak-until-bearing verdict from this campaign's TLSF half: the same wrong answers fed the vacuity, weakening and implication filters. examples/arbiter-aurus/fixes/arbiter_fixed0.tlsf carries a W, so head-to-head relations against that ideal in earlier campaigns want re-checking too.
Timeout caps never bound: 0 rows carry timed_out=1 or compare_timed_out=1 on either path.
The campaign says nothing about intermediate elitism rates. The two arms are the two candidate defaults; no claim about 0.05 or 0.2 follows.
The ltl2tgba orphan-reaper cron was verified installed on both hosts before launch, and both showed zero live ltl2tgba processes at launch.

rows.tlsf_missing_note: 6 runs died on a SPOT build limit, 'Too many acceptance sets used. The limit is 32', treated as fatal by the runner. 4 form complete pairs and drop cleanly; 2 are unpaired (gyro-var1 seed14 elit0, lift seed34 elit0.1). Both arms affected, so the comparison is unbiased.

found_repair.note: interval excludes zero: elitism 0 finds MORE repairs

triviality_audit.method: ltlfilt --equivalent-to=1 over the guarantee formulae of all 9,814 written repairs, lowered with the `ltl` tool; 44,101 formulae, 1,673 distinct. Run offline against the retained run directories, so it could not affect the campaign. Deliberately not counter's own vacuity predicate, which would only confirm the screen agrees with itself.
triviality_audit.cause: Not an elitism effect. black answers a validity query wrong on formulae carrying weak-until: its infinite-trace loop rules treat only F and U as eventualities, so the strong-release its NNF derives from a negated W is never forced to be fulfilled. Fixed in fb4c3ed (PR #95), after this campaign ran. Every one of the 7 would be screened out by a current binary.
